newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Floods seen hitting Slovak wheat harvest - TASR.
newsitem.headline: Floods seen hitting Slovak wheat harvest - TASR.

text.p: Slovakia's wheat harvest, originally estimated at 2.05 million tonnes, will be lower than expected due to heavy rains and flooding over the past two weeks, the official TASR news agency said on Thursday.

Quoting a report by the ministry of agriculture giving a survey of wheat production over the past three years, TASR said the "results of this year's (wheat) harvest are unlikely to fulfill the comparatively optimistic forecasts".
The original per hectare wheat yield estimate for this year was 4.9 tonnes.

Four days before the heavy rains and floods struck on July 12, the Slovak Statistical Bureau (SUSR) said Slovakia's 1997 grain harvest was estimated at up to 3.12 million tonnes, an increase of 19.1 percent over 1996.
The rapeseed harvest was estimated at between 199,000 tonnes and 208,000 tonnes, an increase of 42.6 percent over 1996, SUSR said.
The grain and rapeseed harvest increases were a result of larger sown areas and bigger estimated yields per hectare. The grain estimate did not include seed maize.
TASR said 34,000 hectares of agricultural land was flooded as of July 24 with the Trnava region in southest Slovakia worst hit with 11,000 hectares of agricultural land under water.

TASR said that of the flooded land 15,000 hectares were sown with grain, which was two percent of the overall sown area, 3,600 hectares with maize or 2.6 percent of the overall sown surface, and 980 hectares of sugar beet, or 2.3 percent of the total sown area.
